correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation of the primal Gaussian surface-area density and the exact polar radial function gives the Hessian formula; spherical harmonic diagonalization and a separate integral identity prove the complete sign classification, reproducing the known translated-ball coefficient as a consistency check.

originality.rationale: The September 16, 2026 source computes only the translated-ball degree-one perturbation. Targeted searches and the public SCOPE repository found no full support-function Hessian or spherical-harmonic spectrum for this uncentered Gaussian volume product.

value.rationale: The result identifies the exact spectral mechanism of the phase transition: translations are the sole modes that can destabilize the ball, and they span the entire positive eigenspace above sigma^2=2/(n+1), while all other modes stay negative.
